instruction: Delete the last slide (the Homework slide) from the Forests presentation in LibreOffice Impress.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to use Summary Slide feature in LibreOffice Impress. It navigated to the Slide menu and found the Summary Slide option, but struggled with selecting all slides first. It repeatedly tried Ctrl+A, scrolled through slide panel, and accidentally duplicated slides, ending with 14-15 slides instead of a proper summary. Ran out of 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Impress menus (Slide, Edit, View), click slides in slide panel, scroll through slides, use keyboard shortcuts, access Slide menu options (Duplicate Slide, Delete Slide, New Slide)
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed to properly execute the multi-step Summary Slide workflow. It could not reliably select all slides simultaneously and kept accidentally creating extra slides.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to single slide deletion — the model showed it can navigate to specific slides and access the Slide menu where Delete Slide is available. Tests basic slide management without complex multi-selection.
metadata.explanation: Task requires deleting the last slide (Homework). Getter reads the saved PPTX, checks total slide count (should be 11) and that no slide has title 'Homework:'. Partial credit: 0.5 for correct count, 0.5 for title removal.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the saved PPTX file and extracts slide count and all slide titles, which are the two pieces of state needed to verify the instruction.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses 'expected_slide_count' and 'removed_title' from the rules dict without incorrectly nesting into 'rules' key.
Both instruction requirements are verified: slide count reduced to 11 (from original 12) and 'Homework:' title no longer present, with reasonable 0.5/0.5 partial credit split.
Postconfig correctly activates the Impress window and saves the file with Ctrl+S before the getter reads the PPTX, ensuring fresh file state on disk.

Minor concern: title extraction uses first non-empty text from any shape rather than specifically the title placeholder, which could theoretically pick up non-title text. However, for detecting 'Homework:' presence/absence this is robust enough.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider using shape.shape_id or checking for title placeholder type (shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE) for more precise title extraction, though current approach is adequate for this task.
